pathway.title: Mativ Holdings, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the refinancing changed the shape of the debt more than its size. On April 3, 2026 Mativ replaced its revolver, Term Loan A and Term Loan B and removed the delayed draw term loan, which took away the May 2027 maturity wall (about USD 514.2 million at year-end 2025) [CP-1 debt register; CP-1A transaction summary]. Total debt carrying value is USD 976.4 million and net debt USD 879.1 million, against USD 1,018.2 million and USD 934.0 million at December 31, 2025. The mechanic is that the nearest large repayment is now the notes, which with small amortization make up USD 406.2 million of the USD 1,011.1 million of principal due in 2029 on the maturity table, about 40.2 percent [CP-1 debt maturities chart; calculated below]. The implication is low near-term repayment risk and a concentrated 2029 refinancing, with an eight percent coupon already in the cost of debt. One wording in the credit agreement could pull the revolver and Term Loan A (USD 109.7 million drawn and outstanding) ahead of the notes, which would lift the 2029 bucket to about 51.0 percent of principal; the filing's own maturity table does not show this, and the amended agreement is needed to settle it [CP-0 and CP-1 conflicts].

Second, leverage depends on whose earnings are used, and the deleveraging has mostly come from earnings, not debt paydown. Management states net leverage of 3.8x at September 30, 2026 against 5.00x allowed, down from 4.2x at December 31, 2025 [CP-1 covenants]. On reported operating profit plus depreciation and amortization, net debt to EBITDA fell from 5.54x to 4.19x, and holding net debt at the year-end level would have given 4.45x, so about 1.09x of the 1.35x improvement came from higher trailing EBITDA (USD 168.5 million to USD 210.0 million) and about 0.26x from lower net debt [calculated below]. The mechanic is that trailing EBITDA rose partly because restructuring and impairment charges fell (nine months 2026 USD 4.7 million against USD 18.2 million) and partly on margin recovery; both can reverse. The implication is that leverage headroom today is comfortable (EBITDA could fall about 24.0 percent before 5.00x at constant net debt) but narrows toward the final 4.00x step, where the same measure gives about 5.0 percent, and the step dates are not disclosed [CP-1 covenants].

Third, interest cover is thin on reported earnings. EBITDA covers cash interest 2.62x over the last twelve months and interest expense 2.92x, only 0.12x above the lowest covenant level of 2.50x and below the 3.00x top level, although covenant EBITDA and interest are defined differently and the reported coverage ratio is not disclosed [CP-1 interest cover chart; CP-1 covenants]. Management's own nine-month adjusted EBITDA over cash interest is 3.52x. The mechanic is a fixed interest burden of about USD 80.1 million of cash interest on earnings that move with volume; the implication is limited cushion if the third-quarter volume decline persists.

Fourth, the earnings mix is shifting toward the higher-margin segment while the larger segment weakens. Filtration & Advanced Materials grew net sales 10.2 percent in Q3 2026 with a gross margin of 23.6 percent, while Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions fell 10.9 percent at a gross margin of 16.4 percent, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 62.3 million fell about 7 percent against USD 66.8 million a year earlier [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model]. Price added 3.7 percent to Q3 sales while volume and mix removed 5.9 percent, so margin recovery has come from pricing, not volume. The mechanic is dependence on input-cost pass-through and demand in cyclical end markets, with Healthcare weak. The implication is that a further volume loss would flow disproportionately into earnings and cover.

Fifth, liquidity is adequate but less deep than before and partly dependent on off-balance-sheet funding. Liquidity of USD 373.5 million is cash of USD 97.3 million (USD 72.7 million held abroad) plus printed undrawn revolver capacity of USD 276.2 million, down from USD 498.5 million in March 2026 because the revolver was reduced to USD 305.0 million; USD 8.8 million of commitment is unexplained [CP-1 liquidity]. Trailing free cash flow of about USD 98.5 million after USD 22.5 million of dividends leaves about USD 76.0 million a year, so if that were held flat to October 2029 it would retire about 57 percent of the USD 400.0 million notes [calculated below, assumption stated]. The company sold USD 837.3 million of receivables in nine months 2026 under a program extended to October 23, 2029, and carries leases, pensions and a foreign exchange contract liability outside reported debt [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The implication is that the notes will need refinancing and that withdrawal of the receivables program would need replacement from the revolver.

Sixth, the July 27, 2026 tornado left USD 38.0 million of insurance recoveries receivable (about 39 percent of cash) and a net recorded loss of USD 0.8 million; business interruption recoveries are not recognized. The mechanic is delayed cash on an insured loss and a single third-party distribution node that interrupted supply; the implication is a near-term liquidity watch item, with management expecting full recovery of the inventory loss [CP-1 events; CP-1A operating model, Management Language].

Seventh, creditor protection cannot be read directly. The maintenance covenants are stated to apply to the revolver and Term Loan A only, so the USD 498.7 million Term Loan B carries none; the credit agreement, indenture and receivables agreement are not in the evidence, so baskets, guarantor coverage, security after the amendment and distribution capacity are unknown. Documented actions show no related-party, priming or non-pro rata transactions and a smaller dividend than in 2023 [CP-1A governance]. The implication is a supportive willingness record but an untested legal capacity.

runs.text: Strengths. The business is diversified: no product category exceeds 35 percent of sales and no customer exceeds 10 percent, which supports revenue durability through cycles [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. The capital structure is refinanced, with the nearest large maturity in October 2029, covenant compliance stated at September 30, 2026 and liquidity of USD 373.5 million [CP-1 liquidity and debt register; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation covers capital spending and the dividend: nine-month free cash flow was USD 90.5 million (a management measure) against dividends of USD 17.0 million [CP-1 cash flow; Documentary Fact]. Filtration & Advanced Materials is gaining profitability, with adjusted EBITDA of USD 39.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 32.9 million, and management targets further cost savings of USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million by end 2026 [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact for the first, Management Language for the target]. About two thirds of floating bank debt is hedged with interest rate swaps (USD 405.8 million notional against USD 608.4 million of floating balances), limiting rate sensitivity [CP-1A operating model; Analyst Interpretation on the ratio]. Reporting quality is sound, with effective internal control and no related-party or priming-type transaction found [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. Reported leverage and cover are tight: net debt to EBITDA of 4.19x and EBITDA to cash interest of 2.62x on reported earnings, with total debt to capital at 67.6 percent [CP-1 leverage and covenants; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Margins are low and recovered through price while volume and mix fell, with the larger segment, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, at a lower gross margin and showing a 10.9 percent sales decline in Q3 2026 [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Refinancing is back-ended: the USD 400.0 million notes at 8.000% fall due on October 1, 2029, and a possible earlier maturity of the revolver and Term Loan A is unresolved [CP-1 debt maturities; Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information]. Funding relies on a receivables program that is off balance sheet and on claims outside reported debt, including operating leases of USD 56.2 million, pension and other postretirement liabilities of USD 49.1 million and a foreign exchange contract liability of USD 27.6 million [CP-1 claims outside debt; Documentary Fact]. Operating concentration was demonstrated by the tornado, and Healthcare volume is weak [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].

runs.text: The one financing transaction in the period is the Ninth Amendment of April 3, 2026 to the 2018 multicurrency credit agreement (the ninth amendment, after an Eighth Amendment dated December 17, 2024). Status: executed, effective April 3, 2026, reported in the 10-Q Q1 as a subsequent event and in the 10-Q Q2 and Q3 as completed (10-Q Q1 page:21; 10-Q Q3 page:13). It provided a 305.0 revolving facility with euro and sterling sub-facilities, an 89.9 Term Loan A and a 500.0 Term Loan B, 894.9 of committed facilities in total, and eliminated the delayed draw term loan. Use of proceeds is shown in the cash flow statement: nine-month debt proceeds of 705.7 against repayments of 728.1, 32.7 of issuance costs and an 8.7 loss on debt extinguishment. The revolver and Term Loan A mature on the earlier of five years from April 3, 2026 or 182 days before the notes' maturity, and the Term Loan B on the earlier of seven years or 91 days before it; certain subsidiaries became additional U.S. borrowers and another a guarantor (names not supplied). The Term Loan B pays fixed margins of 3.50 to 4.50 percent depending on the benchmark, against 2.75 percent over Term SOFR and 3.75 percent over EURIBOR in the 10-K description of the prior agreement, which reads as roughly 75 basis points more at the stated ends, although the 10-Q does not say which end applies to which benchmark. This is an Analyst Interpretation. Liquidity effect: revolver availability dropped from 416.2 (old 600.0 facility, March 31, 2026) to 279.2 at June 30, 2026, and total liquidity from 498.5 to 345.5, in exchange for the removal of the May 2027 maturity wall (10-K page:103 shows 514.2 of maturities in 2027).

New debt issues in the supplied sources: none in the twelve months to the cutoff other than the refinancing; the 400.0 of 8.000% senior unsecured notes due October 1, 2029 were issued in a Rule 144A and Regulation S private offering on October 7, 2024 and remain outstanding, redeemable from October 1, 2026 at indenture prices not supplied (10-Q Q3 page:12). The use of proceeds of the 2024 notes is Not supplied in the sources. The 10-K shows 2024 debt proceeds of 531.0 and repayments of 554.7 and a 7.3 loss on debt extinguishment (10-K page:75, page:78).

Other transactions with creditor consequences. The Engineered Papers sale on November 30, 2023 to Evergreen Hill Enterprise Pte. Ltd. for 620.0 in cash was followed by a debt repayment of about 641.2 that the 10-K says was based on the triggering of a financial covenant in the loan agreement, and Mativ retains an indemnity capped at 10 with no material claims pending (10-K page:95; 10-Q Q3 page:17); this made the company smaller and ended tobacco exposure. The Neenah merger of July 6, 2022 created the current company. On October 23, 2026 the Receivables Sales Agreement was amended to extend its term to October 23, 2029 (it previously ran through November 5, 2026 with a maximum funding commitment of 150.0; the post-amendment commitment is Not supplied). On November 4, 2026 a held-for-sale North American facility was sold; proceeds are Not supplied and accumulated restructuring charges on the site were 7.9 (10-Q Q3 page:11, page:23). The July 27, 2026 tornado is an operating event with an open insurance claim, not a financing transaction, and is described in the CP-1 handoff.

fields.value: The module extracts the statement lines the credit view needs, builds the debt, liquidity, covenant and off-debt claim registers, and computes leverage and cover on stated bases. It hands readiness, limits and gaps to the next modules. Abbreviations used in locators: 10-K is the FY2025 annual report; 10-Q Q1, Q2 and Q3 are the 2026 quarterly reports; Release Q1, Q2 and Q3 are the 2026 earnings release exhibits; `page:N` is the source chunk number, not the printed page.

Statement values were read from the page text and checked by tie-outs in Calculations; no image or chart content exists in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For Mativ Holdings, Inc. the financial base at September 30, 2026 is a company with USD 1,510.9 million of nine-month net sales (nine months 2026), gross profit up year on year for the nine months (though down in Q3), a thin operating margin and a net loss close to break-even for the nine months (net loss of 9.3 against a prior-year loss of 438.2 that carried an 411.9 goodwill impairment), financed by 976.4 of total debt (carrying value, net of 34.7 issuance costs; principal 1,011.1) against cash and cash equivalents of 97.3, so reported net debt of 879.1. The structure was reset on April 3, 2026 by the Ninth Amendment: a 305.0 revolver (20.0 drawn), an 89.9 Term Loan A, a 500.0 Term Loan B and the unchanged 400.0 of 8.000% senior unsecured notes due October 1, 2029. Management states net leverage of 3.8x at September 30, 2026 against a current maximum of 5.00x, down from 4.2x at December 31, 2025 and 4.1x at March 31, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reported-basis measures built here are lower quality than management's: operating profit plus depreciation and amortization (with the 411.9 FY2025 goodwill impairment added back) gives trailing EBITDA of 210.0 at Q3 2026, so total debt to EBITDA is 4.65x and net debt to EBITDA is 4.19x, with EBITDA to cash interest of 2.62x. These are above management's 3.8x because the credit agreement and management adjusted EBITDA add back items such as stock compensation, restructuring, financing fees on the receivables program and purchase-accounting items; that definition is not supplied, so the two cannot be reconciled and neither is restated into the other. Evidence to risk to implication: a lender that sizes debt on the adjusted figure sees a levered but compliant credit; a lender that sizes it on reported earnings sees a leverage multiple that only recently dropped below five times, which makes the 2029 notes refinancing and the covenant step-downs the focus.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is cash of 97.3 plus printed undrawn revolver capacity of 276.2, total 373.5, down from 498.5 at March 31, 2026 because the revolver was cut from 600.0 to 305.0. On the maturity table's reading nothing in the debt falls due before 2029 except 2.2 in the rest of 2026 and small amortization. Claims outside the debt figure are meaningful: a receivables sale program (837.3 sold in nine months 2026, balance outstanding not supplied), a foreign exchange contract liability of 27.6 in other liabilities (the euro cross-currency swap hedges are disclosed alongside), pension and other postretirement liabilities of 49.1, operating leases of 56.2, finance leases of 14.7 non-current, purchase obligations of 105.1 at year-end 2025, and open insurance recovery on the July 27, 2026 Menasha tornado (expense of 43.8 less recoveries received 5.0 and receivable 38.0, leaving a 0.8 net loss recorded). The view is restricted by the absence of the credit agreement, the indenture, the receivables agreement and any annual adjusted EBITDA.

Definitions that differ from the metric computed here: the covenant ratio uses the agreement's EBITDA and net debt, while the reported-basis EBITDA here is operating profit plus cash flow D&A with the FY2025 goodwill impairment added back and no other adjustments. A back-solve of the stated 3.8x on the release's net debt of 879.1 implies covenant EBITDA of roughly 231 (range 228 to 234 for ratios of 3.85x to 3.75x), about 21 above the reported-basis 210.0; this is an inference that assumes the covenant net debt equals the release net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For Mativ Holdings, Inc. the creditor-relevant facts are these. It is a publicly listed Delaware company (NYSE: MATV) that has been independent since a 1995 spin-off from Kimberly-Clark and took its current form on July 6, 2022 when Schweitzer-Mauduit International merged with Neenah and renamed itself Mativ. Its 2023 sale of the Engineered Papers business for 620.0 in cash ended participation in tobacco-based product markets and was followed by a debt repayment of about 641.2 that the 10-K ties to a covenant trigger. There is no sponsor, and no controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied text (Part III of the 10-K is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not in the sources), so ownership behaviour can only be judged from documented issuer actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating model: two reportable segments, Filtration & Advanced Materials (FAM, about 39 percent of FY2025 revenue) and Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions (SAS, about 61 percent), serve dozens of end markets through 34 production locations on three continents and sales in more than 100 countries, with roughly 57 percent of Q3 2026 net sales to U.S. customers and 25 percent to Europe. The risk mechanics that matter to a creditor are: pricing power against resin, fiber, pulp and energy inputs (selling prices rose in 2026 while volume and mix fell), a weakening SAS volume position in Q3 2026 (tornado and Healthcare) set against FAM growth, a margin structure in which FAM earns materially higher gross margin than SAS, and a funding model that sells receivables off balance sheet and relies on a revolver that is now 305.0. Credit implication: revenue is diversified and customer-qualified, which supports durability, but gross margin of roughly 19.6 percent for nine months 2026 and reported-basis interest cover of 2.62x leave little room for a volume shock; the July 27, 2026 tornado showed that a single third-party distribution node can interrupt supply for a whole product line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Transactions: the April 3, 2026 Ninth Amendment refinanced the entire bank group (revolver cut from 600.0 to 305.0, Term Loan A 89.9, Term Loan B 500.0, delayed draw term loan removed, maturities moved from May 2027 to 2031 and 2033 on the stated terms, subject to a springing wording that is unresolved against the maturity table). The 400.0 of 8.000% senior unsecured notes issued in October 2024 are the nearest maturity on the company's own statements (October 1, 2029). The interaction between the term loan B's size and the covenant scope is the main structural point: the maintenance covenants are stated to apply to the revolver and Term Loan A only, so the 500.0 Term Loan B lenders hold no maintenance test of their own. Restrictions on information: the credit agreement, indenture and receivables agreement are not supplied, so baskets, guarantor coverage and restricted payment capacity are Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one financing transaction in the period is the Ninth Amendment of April 3, 2026 to the 2018 multicurrency credit agreement (the ninth amendment, after an Eighth Amendment dated December 17, 2024). Status: executed, effective April 3, 2026, reported in the 10-Q Q1 as a subsequent event and in the 10-Q Q2 and Q3 as completed (10-Q Q1 page:21; 10-Q Q3 page:13). It provided a 305.0 revolving facility with euro and sterling sub-facilities, an 89.9 Term Loan A and a 500.0 Term Loan B, 894.9 of committed facilities in total, and eliminated the delayed draw term loan. Use of proceeds is shown in the cash flow statement: nine-month debt proceeds of 705.7 against repayments of 728.1, 32.7 of issuance costs and an 8.7 loss on debt extinguishment. The revolver and Term Loan A mature on the earlier of five years from April 3, 2026 or 182 days before the notes' maturity, and the Term Loan B on the earlier of seven years or 91 days before it; certain subsidiaries became additional U.S. borrowers and another a guarantor (names not supplied). The Term Loan B pays fixed margins of 3.50 to 4.50 percent depending on the benchmark, against 2.75 percent over Term SOFR and 3.75 percent over EURIBOR in the 10-K description of the prior agreement, which reads as roughly 75 basis points more at the stated ends, although the 10-Q does not say which end applies to which benchmark. This is an Analyst Interpretation. Liquidity effect: revolver availability dropped from 416.2 (old 600.0 facility, March 31, 2026) to 279.2 at June 30, 2026, and total liquidity from 498.5 to 345.5, in exchange for the removal of the May 2027 maturity wall (10-K page:103 shows 514.2 of maturities in 2027).

fields.value: New debt issues in the supplied sources: none in the twelve months to the cutoff other than the refinancing; the 400.0 of 8.000% senior unsecured notes due October 1, 2029 were issued in a Rule 144A and Regulation S private offering on October 7, 2024 and remain outstanding, redeemable from October 1, 2026 at indenture prices not supplied (10-Q Q3 page:12). The use of proceeds of the 2024 notes is Not supplied in the sources. The 10-K shows 2024 debt proceeds of 531.0 and repayments of 554.7 and a 7.3 loss on debt extinguishment (10-K page:75, page:78).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions with creditor consequences. The Engineered Papers sale on November 30, 2023 to Evergreen Hill Enterprise Pte. Ltd. for 620.0 in cash was followed by a debt repayment of about 641.2 that the 10-K says was based on the triggering of a financial covenant in the loan agreement, and Mativ retains an indemnity capped at 10 with no material claims pending (10-K page:95; 10-Q Q3 page:17); this made the company smaller and ended tobacco exposure. The Neenah merger of July 6, 2022 created the current company. On October 23, 2026 the Receivables Sales Agreement was amended to extend its term to October 23, 2029 (it previously ran through November 5, 2026 with a maximum funding commitment of 150.0; the post-amendment commitment is Not supplied). On November 4, 2026 a held-for-sale North American facility was sold; proceeds are Not supplied and accumulated restructuring charges on the site were 7.9 (10-Q Q3 page:11, page:23). The July 27, 2026 tornado is an operating event with an open insurance claim, not a financing transaction, and is described in the CP-1 handoff.

fields.value: This credit synthesis covers Mativ Holdings, Inc. (ticker MATV) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway. It builds the fundamental credit view from the financial and business handoffs already accepted, for the reporting currency USD and the periods Q3 2026 and FY2025. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mativ Holdings, Inc. is a leveraged but liquid specialty materials credit whose fundamental strength is adequate and improving, not yet comfortable. Its strongest support is a refinanced capital structure with no material maturity before the USD 400.0 million 8.000% notes due October 1, 2029, USD 373.5 million of liquidity and compliance with a net leverage covenant that stands at 3.8x against a 5.00x maximum. Its weakest point is thin earnings coverage: on reported earnings net debt is 4.19x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.62x, while the largest segment by revenue, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, earns the lower gross margin and lost volume in the third quarter of 2026. The outcome turns on whether price-led margin recovery and cost savings hold as volume weakens, and on refinancing the 2029 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the refinancing changed the shape of the debt more than its size. On April 3, 2026 Mativ replaced its revolver, Term Loan A and Term Loan B and removed the delayed draw term loan, which took away the May 2027 maturity wall (about USD 514.2 million at year-end 2025) [CP-1 debt register; CP-1A transaction summary]. Total debt carrying value is USD 976.4 million and net debt USD 879.1 million, against USD 1,018.2 million and USD 934.0 million at December 31, 2025. The mechanic is that the nearest large repayment is now the notes, which with small amortization make up USD 406.2 million of the USD 1,011.1 million of principal due in 2029 on the maturity table, about 40.2 percent [CP-1 debt maturities chart; calculated below]. The implication is low near-term repayment risk and a concentrated 2029 refinancing, with an eight percent coupon already in the cost of debt. One wording in the credit agreement could pull the revolver and Term Loan A (USD 109.7 million drawn and outstanding) ahead of the notes, which would lift the 2029 bucket to about 51.0 percent of principal; the filing's own maturity table does not show this, and the amended agreement is needed to settle it [CP-0 and CP-1 conflicts].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, leverage depends on whose earnings are used, and the deleveraging has mostly come from earnings, not debt paydown. Management states net leverage of 3.8x at September 30, 2026 against 5.00x allowed, down from 4.2x at December 31, 2025 [CP-1 covenants]. On reported operating profit plus depreciation and amortization, net debt to EBITDA fell from 5.54x to 4.19x, and holding net debt at the year-end level would have given 4.45x, so about 1.09x of the 1.35x improvement came from higher trailing EBITDA (USD 168.5 million to USD 210.0 million) and about 0.26x from lower net debt [calculated below]. The mechanic is that trailing EBITDA rose partly because restructuring and impairment charges fell (nine months 2026 USD 4.7 million against USD 18.2 million) and partly on margin recovery; both can reverse. The implication is that leverage headroom today is comfortable (EBITDA could fall about 24.0 percent before 5.00x at constant net debt) but narrows toward the final 4.00x step, where the same measure gives about 5.0 percent, and the step dates are not disclosed [CP-1 covenants].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, interest cover is thin on reported earnings. EBITDA covers cash interest 2.62x over the last twelve months and interest expense 2.92x, only 0.12x above the lowest covenant level of 2.50x and below the 3.00x top level, although covenant EBITDA and interest are defined differently and the reported coverage ratio is not disclosed [CP-1 interest cover chart; CP-1 covenants]. Management's own nine-month adjusted EBITDA over cash interest is 3.52x. The mechanic is a fixed interest burden of about USD 80.1 million of cash interest on earnings that move with volume; the implication is limited cushion if the third-quarter volume decline persists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, the earnings mix is shifting toward the higher-margin segment while the larger segment weakens. Filtration & Advanced Materials grew net sales 10.2 percent in Q3 2026 with a gross margin of 23.6 percent, while Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions fell 10.9 percent at a gross margin of 16.4 percent, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 62.3 million fell about 7 percent against USD 66.8 million a year earlier [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model]. Price added 3.7 percent to Q3 sales while volume and mix removed 5.9 percent, so margin recovery has come from pricing, not volume. The mechanic is dependence on input-cost pass-through and demand in cyclical end markets, with Healthcare weak. The implication is that a further volume loss would flow disproportionately into earnings and cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, liquidity is adequate but less deep than before and partly dependent on off-balance-sheet funding. Liquidity of USD 373.5 million is cash of USD 97.3 million (USD 72.7 million held abroad) plus printed undrawn revolver capacity of USD 276.2 million, down from USD 498.5 million in March 2026 because the revolver was reduced to USD 305.0 million; USD 8.8 million of commitment is unexplained [CP-1 liquidity]. Trailing free cash flow of about USD 98.5 million after USD 22.5 million of dividends leaves about USD 76.0 million a year, so if that were held flat to October 2029 it would retire about 57 percent of the USD 400.0 million notes [calculated below, assumption stated]. The company sold USD 837.3 million of receivables in nine months 2026 under a program extended to October 23, 2029, and carries leases, pensions and a foreign exchange contract liability outside reported debt [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The implication is that the notes will need refinancing and that withdrawal of the receivables program would need replacement from the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the July 27, 2026 tornado left USD 38.0 million of insurance recoveries receivable (about 39 percent of cash) and a net recorded loss of USD 0.8 million; business interruption recoveries are not recognized. The mechanic is delayed cash on an insured loss and a single third-party distribution node that interrupted supply; the implication is a near-term liquidity watch item, with management expecting full recovery of the inventory loss [CP-1 events; CP-1A operating model, Management Language].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, creditor protection cannot be read directly. The maintenance covenants are stated to apply to the revolver and Term Loan A only, so the USD 498.7 million Term Loan B carries none; the credit agreement, indenture and receivables agreement are not in the evidence, so baskets, guarantor coverage, security after the amendment and distribution capacity are unknown. Documented actions show no related-party, priming or non-pro rata transactions and a smaller dividend than in 2023 [CP-1A governance]. The implication is a supportive willingness record but an untested legal capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The business is diversified: no product category exceeds 35 percent of sales and no customer exceeds 10 percent, which supports revenue durability through cycles [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. The capital structure is refinanced, with the nearest large maturity in October 2029, covenant compliance stated at September 30, 2026 and liquidity of USD 373.5 million [CP-1 liquidity and debt register; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation covers capital spending and the dividend: nine-month free cash flow was USD 90.5 million (a management measure) against dividends of USD 17.0 million [CP-1 cash flow; Documentary Fact]. Filtration & Advanced Materials is gaining profitability, with adjusted EBITDA of USD 39.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 32.9 million, and management targets further cost savings of USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million by end 2026 [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact for the first, Management Language for the target]. About two thirds of floating bank debt is hedged with interest rate swaps (USD 405.8 million notional against USD 608.4 million of floating balances), limiting rate sensitivity [CP-1A operating model; Analyst Interpretation on the ratio]. Reporting quality is sound, with effective internal control and no related-party or priming-type transaction found [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Reported leverage and cover are tight: net debt to EBITDA of 4.19x and EBITDA to cash interest of 2.62x on reported earnings, with total debt to capital at 67.6 percent [CP-1 leverage and covenants; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Margins are low and recovered through price while volume and mix fell, with the larger segment, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, at a lower gross margin and showing a 10.9 percent sales decline in Q3 2026 [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Refinancing is back-ended: the USD 400.0 million notes at 8.000% fall due on October 1, 2029, and a possible earlier maturity of the revolver and Term Loan A is unresolved [CP-1 debt maturities; Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information]. Funding relies on a receivables program that is off balance sheet and on claims outside reported debt, including operating leases of USD 56.2 million, pension and other postretirement liabilities of USD 49.1 million and a foreign exchange contract liability of USD 27.6 million [CP-1 claims outside debt; Documentary Fact]. Operating concentration was demonstrated by the tornado, and Healthcare volume is weak [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].
